card.name: Capital K starting brand drug names
card.fires_on: The letter K (often with a leading space) that begins a brand-name drug written in capitals or as a new name, such as KALYDECO, KESIMPTA, KRYSTEXXA. It appears after words like of, with, take, or stopping.

modes.label: Capitalized brand names
modes.description: K opens an all-caps brand name in prescribing text, right after a verb or preposition.
modes.example: The recommended dosage of<< K>>ALYDECO for adults and pediatric

modes.label: Other K names
modes.description: K starts a brand or medical name in running text, such as Klonopin or Kaposi.

card.writes: It promotes odd name-like pieces and suppresses 'g' endings, so it mainly pushes the model to continue a new proper name.
card.plain: It lights up on the first letter K of a brand drug name like Kalydeco, when the name is about to be spelled out.
